turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from device physics and training patterns

**What the training data rewards (n-i-p MAPbI3):**
- **SnO2-based or fullerene-modified compact ETLs** — best band alignment (deep CB, high mobility, low-temperature, fewer UV traps than TiO2): TiO2-c|SnO2-np/Spiro/Ag = **20.85%**, SnO2-c|PCBM/Spiro = 17.3–18.0%, TiO2-c|C60/PTAA/Ag = **16.5%**.
- **Passivating interlayers under Spiro-MeOTAD** (PMMA|Spiro 18.0, PbS-QDs|Spiro 18.6, IEICO-4F|Spiro 19.0) — suppress interface recombination at the perovskite/HTL contact.
- **Doped small-molecule stacks via co-evaporation**: C60;PhIm|C60 / TaTm:F6-TCNNQ = **17.9%** — excellent selectivity, conformal pinhole-free films.
- **PCBM ETL + wide-gap polymer HTM + MoO3/Au**: TiO2-c|PCBM-60 / PCDTBT1 / MoO3|Au = **19.35%** (best-in-class hole selectivity plus good electron extraction).
- Au/Ag back contacts with oxide buffers; plain TiO2-mp/carbon and exotic contacts score low.

**Matching pool candidates:**
- **c064** (TiO2-c|SnO2-np / Spiro / Au): near-replica of the 20.85% champion recipe and the 17.47% TiO2-c|SnO2 analog — SnO2 interlayer passivates TiO2 surface traps and improves electron extraction. Top pick.
- **c005** (TiO2-c|PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3|Au): direct homolog of the 19.35% PCDTBT1 device — same selective-contact physics, only a polymer variant.
- **c017** (C60;PhIm|C60 / TaTm:F6-TCNNQ / co-evaporation): near-identical to the 17.9% co-evaporated stack (Ag instead of Au) — doped, fully vacuum-processed selective contacts.
- **c043** (TiO2-mp + DAHI|Spiro): ammonium-halide surface passivation before Spiro mirrors the PMMA|Spiro (18.0%) and QD|Spiro (18.6%) passivation motif — reduced interface recombination, higher Voc.
- **c073** (TiO2-c|C60 / PTAA / Ag): exact match to the 16.5% training row, with an HMDS scaffold that should aid film wetting/grain growth.

Runners-up considered and rejected: c068 (train shows PTAA with Au|MoO3 order underperforming), c031/c025 (good SnO2 stacks but no passivation edge), c080/c015 (fullerene ETLs ~15–16%).

**Final: c064, c005, c017, c043, c073**
